record.context_brief: Meaning of the spectrum of KK* for planar bipartite graphs
record.original_question: For a bipartite planar graph, choose any Kasteleyn matrix K obtained from the bipartite adjacency matrix by changing signs so that all non-zero determinant contributions have the same sign. Determine the combinatorial significance of the spectrum of KK*, which is independent of the particular Kasteleyn signing.

evidence.quote: However, the spectrum of K times its adjoint K* is independent of which Kasteleyn matrix K one chooses (independently shown by David Wilson and Horst Sachs). Thus, it is natural to ask:
Problem 6: What is the significance of the spectrum of KK*, where K is any Kasteleyn matrix associated with a bipartite planar graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (B \sqcup W, E)$ be a finite bipartite planar graph with equal-sized color classes $|B| = |W| = n$, embedded in the plane. The bipartite adjacency matrix $A$ of $G$ is the $n \times n$ matrix indexed by $B \times W$ with $A_{bw} = 1$ if $bw \in E$ and $0$ otherwise. A Kasteleyn signing of $G$ is an assignment $\varepsilon : E \to \{+1, -1\}$ such that around every bounded face with $2k$ edges, the product of the signs is $(-1)^{k+1}$; given such a signing, the associated Kasteleyn matrix $K$ is the $n \times n$ matrix with $K_{bw} = \varepsilon(bw)$ if $bw \in E$ and $0$ otherwise. With this normalization every nonzero term in the expansion of $\det K$ contributes with the same sign, so $|\det K|$ equals the number of perfect matchings of $G$.

It is known that, although $K$ depends on the choice of Kasteleyn signing, the spectrum of $K K^{*}$ (equivalently, the multiset of singular values of $K$) does not depend on this choice; it is an invariant of the planar bipartite graph $G$ itself.

Problem. Give a combinatorial interpretation of the spectrum of $K K^{*}$ for an arbitrary planar bipartite graph $G$: identify the eigenvalues (with multiplicities) of $K K^{*}$ in terms of intrinsic combinatorial or graph-theoretic data of $G$ (such as counts or generating functions involving subgraphs, matchings, cycles, faces, or related structures).
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive combinatorial interpretation of the spectrum of $KK^{*}$ for general planar bipartite graphs. Related work on dimer models, Kasteleyn theorem and spectral aspects of Kasteleyn operators exists (e.g., spectral curves for periodic bipartite graphs and Kenyon–Okounkov–Sheffield theory), but no source found explicitly resolves the general combinatorial significance of the spectrum of $KK^{*}$ for arbitrary planar bipartite graphs. The status is therefore unclear.

status_evidence.title: The geometry of dimer models (Cimasoni)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Kasteleyn matrices, signings, and dimer partition functions for planar bipartite graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Survey of Kasteleyn theory does not provide a combinatorial interpretation of the spectrum of KK* in the general planar bipartite setting.

status_evidence.title: Lecture notes on the dimer model (Toninelli)
status_evidence.snippet: Spectral methods diagonalize Kasteleyn matrices for periodic bipartite planar graphs via Fourier analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral results are obtained for periodic graphs but not as a general combinatorial interpretation for arbitrary planar bipartite graphs.

status_evidence.title: Kasteleyn Theorem, Geometric Signatures and KP-II Divisors on Planar Bipartite Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Maximal minors of Kasteleyn sign matrices count dimer configurations with prescribed boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explores algebraic-geometric meaning of Kasteleyn data but does not identify the eigenvalues of KK* combinatorially in general.
